analyst_view.overall: Lugano top the Conference League table with 9 points from 3 games (11 scored), while Jablonec are 23rd on 2 points with no win yet after a 1-1 at Riga, so they need points to stay in the race for the top 24. Lugano beat Grasshopper on Saturday and go to Lucerne on Sunday, so Mattia Croci-Torti may rotate as he did in Europe before. The key point: on 23 November the Swiss league cut Albian Ajeti's ban to two games and both RSI and Bluewin confirm it is domestic only, so he can play in Jablonec, while the numbers take him out as suspended (about -16% on Lugano's goals). Jablonec are without keeper Jan Hanuš (Klemen Mihelak deputises) and Kevin-Prince Milla, both counted, with captain Nemanja Tekijaški's fitness the main question. Referee David Šmajc (6.0 cards a game in a small sample) is already in the numbers.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.1 goals but take about 16% off Lugano's scoring for Ajeti as suspended. RSI and Bluewin both report his ban was cut to two domestic games and he is available on Thursday, so I add most of that back, to about 3.3; not all of it, as Croci-Torti could still rest him with Lucerne on Sunday.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.0 corners, 5.3 for Jablonec, who will push at home as they need a first win. Ajeti's return changes Lugano's finishing rather than how much of the ball they have, so I stay at 9.0.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.2 cards, already adding about 6% for referee David Šmajc, who has shown 6.0 a game in his two on record. Ajeti's red card at St. Gallen was a domestic matter and nothing points to an unusually heated game, so I stay at 5.2.

shots.text: The numbers say 30.6 shots, a fairly open game. Ajeti's return helps Lugano's finishing more than their volume of shots, and possible Lugano rotation before Lucerne pulls the other way, so I stay at 30.6.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.2 shots on target. Jablonec's stand-in keeper Mihelak and Ajeti's availability matter more for goals than for shots on target, so I stay at 9.2.
